## SC-1 (adopted as the new PRIMARY lever, D0) — the biggest change

The critic surfaced a cheaper and strictly stronger lever the plan had missed:
add `junit_family = "xunit1"` to `[tool.pytest.ini_options]` in pyproject.toml.
A CLI `-o` overrides ini, so the canonical launchers are untouched; the gate's
shell launchers are the only junit producers that hand-write the flags; therefore
the ini default is a behavioral no-op everywhere EXCEPT the trap case, where it
makes an omitted flag HARMLESS instead of merely detected. Instance B becomes a
non-event (usable junit, zero re-run) rather than a fast-named failure needing a
scoped re-run — and it protects composition paths nobody has written yet.

Premises independently re-verified by the orchestrator before adoption: the ini
table exists with testpaths/addopts/markers and carries no junit_family key; and
the only other junit producer, run_pytest's internal spawn, is already pinned via
the PYTEST_BASE_FLAGS constant, so nothing else changes behavior.

D0 does not satisfy AC3 on its own (AC3 asks for a refusal), so D1 stays. D3 is
demoted from primary detection to insurance.

## SC-2 (adopted) — corrects a factual error in v2

v2 justified D1's scope by claiming the compare invocation at 13-step-9.md L3630
carries no junit path. Wrong: it DOES carry --junitxml (it consumes the junit
rather than producing it), so piping that correct command through the new guard
would have refused it. v3 scopes the guard to PYTEST launcher text and makes the
consumer exemption explicit rather than emergent. New SC-1 criterion asserts the
consumer command exits 0.
